title: Three Days to the Sahara
summary: Mountain passes, earthen kasbahs and an evening beside the dunes of Erg Chebbi. Three days from Marrakech for those who have always wanted to see the Sahara.
fit: A short stay in Marrakech with the Sahara high on your wish list. You’ll need to be comfortable with long drives, particularly on the final day.
itinerary: Marrakech → Dades Valley
Leave Marrakech early and climb into the High Atlas. Explore Aït Ben Haddou, then continue through the Ouarzazate region and Valley of Roses to a guesthouse in the Dades Valley.
Dades → Todra → Merzouga
Stretch your legs beneath the cliffs of Todra Gorge before continuing east. Arrive at Erg Chebbi as the light changes across the dunes, with the evening to settle into camp.
Merzouga → Marrakech
Set off early for Marrakech, watching the landscapes of southern Morocco unfold again on the return. This is the longest day on the road, so keep your evening unhurried.
practical: The return usually involves around 9–10 hours of driving, plus longer stops. Leave that evening free and avoid a flight connection on the same day. We’ll agree your camp facilities and camel or 4×4 transfer before booking.

story:
The road south is part of the pleasure: the folds of the High Atlas, the warm earth of Aït Ben Haddou and the tall walls of Todra Gorge. By the second evening, the landscape opens into dunes and the pace finally slows.

Spend a night near Erg Chebbi before the long road back to Marrakech. This is a full three days, with plenty of time on the road. If you can spare two more, our slower Sahara route gives you a whole day to enjoy the desert.

title: Imperial Cities & Sahara Nights
summary: From the courtyards of Fes to the dunes of Erg Chebbi, discover Morocco’s cities and southern landscapes on a nine-day journey from Casablanca to Marrakech.
fit: A first visit with a love of history, architecture and changing scenery. Full days in Fes and Marrakech give you time to settle into each city.
itinerary: Casablanca → Rabat
Meet in Casablanca and continue to Rabat. If your arrival time allows, enjoy a first look around Casablanca before heading to the capital.
Rabat → Meknes → Fes
Spend time in Rabat before continuing through Meknes and the Roman remains at Volubilis. Arrive in Fes for the night.
A day in Fes
Explore Fes on foot, moving between historic buildings, working craft shops and the everyday life of the medina.
Fes → Erfoud
Cross the Middle Atlas and follow the Ziz Valley toward Erfoud, where the scenery begins to take on the colors of the desert.
Erfoud → Erg Chebbi
Travel through the Tafilalt region to Merzouga. Reach the Erg Chebbi dunes for an evening at camp.
Merzouga → Dades
Leave the dunes behind and pause in Todra Gorge on the way to your next night in the Dades Valley.
Dades → Marrakech
Visit Aït Ben Haddou before crossing the High Atlas, arriving in Marrakech on the other side of the mountains.
A day in Marrakech
Spend the day among gardens, historic courtyards and souks, with room to follow the parts of Marrakech that interest you most.
Departure
Enjoy your last moments in Morocco before a transfer arranged around your flight or onward plans.
practical: The drives from Fes toward the desert and from Dades to Marrakech take much of the day. Monument and mosque visits follow local opening rules. An extra desert night is an option if you’d like a gentler pace.

story:
Begin among the streets and monuments of Morocco’s imperial cities, where a doorway or a small workshop can be as absorbing as a famous landmark. A full day in Fes leaves time to explore its workshops, courtyards and neighborhoods in depth.

Then travel south through mountain country and the Ziz Valley for an evening in the Sahara. Kasbahs and the High Atlas lead you on to Marrakech, with another full day to explore before you leave.

title: The Sahara, a Little Slower
summary: Two nights near Merzouga and a whole day with the dunes. Take five days from Marrakech to enjoy the Sahara, the southern valleys and the places in between.
fit: Couples, photographers and anyone who would rather linger in the desert. The extra day gives the journey more breathing room, though there are still long drives.
itinerary: Marrakech → Dades
Cross the Atlas and walk through Aït Ben Haddou before continuing into the southern valleys. Spend your first night in Dades.
Dades → Merzouga
Pause beneath the cliffs of Todra Gorge, then head east to Erg Chebbi for your first evening near the dunes.
A day around Erg Chebbi
Explore Khamlia and nearby oasis settlements, or leave the afternoon free to enjoy the dunes. A second night in the region means there’s no need to pack up just yet.
Merzouga → Ouarzazate
Travel through Rissani and the Draa Valley, breaking the return journey with a night near Ouarzazate.
Ouarzazate → Marrakech
Follow the road over the High Atlas, with stops at viewpoints as conditions allow, before returning to Marrakech.
practical: The first and fourth days cover considerable distances. Your two desert nights can be in a camp, a lodge or a combination of both; we’ll set out the options before you book.

story:
The first evening in the desert is only the beginning. With two nights near Erg Chebbi, there’s time to visit Khamlia, explore the surrounding settlements or simply watch the light move across the sand.

The journey home follows the Draa Valley, with a night near Ouarzazate before the Atlas crossing. Choose a camp, a lodge or a night in each—the right combination depends on how you like to spend your evenings.

title: Marrakech to Fes, via the Sahara
summary: Let the journey between two great medinas take you through kasbahs, gorges and the Sahara. Four days, with two nights near Merzouga and a full day around the dunes.
fit: A natural choice if you’re continuing from Marrakech to Fes and want to see the Sahara along the way. The route can also be requested in reverse.
itinerary: Marrakech → Dades
Cross Tizi n’Tichka and visit Aït Ben Haddou before continuing through kasbah country to the Dades Valley for the night.
Dades → Merzouga
Travel through Todra Gorge to the dunes of Erg Chebbi. Your camp transfer will be arranged by camel or 4×4, according to your preference and confirmed plans.
Erg Chebbi at your pace
Visit Khamlia and the surrounding desert region, with time to return to the dunes. Spend a second night near Merzouga.
Merzouga → Fes
Follow the Ziz Valley north through Midelt and the Middle Atlas. Reach Fes in the evening, ready for the next part of your stay.
practical: The first and final days involve long drives. Keep your arrival evening in Fes flexible, and allow extra time before any onward flight.

story:
Leave Marrakech across the Atlas and spend the first night in Dades. Beyond Todra Gorge, the road leads toward Merzouga and the broad sands of Erg Chebbi.

Two nights in the desert region leave a day for Khamlia, nearby settlements and quiet time at the dunes. Then follow the Ziz Valley and Middle Atlas north to Fes, arriving somewhere entirely different from where you began.

title: A Week in Southern Morocco
summary: Stay among kasbahs, palm groves and valley landscapes before reaching the Sahara. A week from Marrakech with two nights near the dunes and time for the road south.
fit: For those drawn to landscapes, small settlements and the south’s earthen architecture. A gradual approach to the Sahara with fewer city changes.
itinerary: Marrakech → Aït Ben Haddou
Take your time crossing the High Atlas and stay near Aït Ben Haddou, with its earthen buildings rising above the valley.
Aït Ben Haddou → Skoura
Continue through Ouarzazate to Skoura, where palm groves bring a welcome change of scenery.
Skoura → Dades
Follow the Valley of Roses toward Dades and settle in for the night among the southern valleys.
Dades → Merzouga
Pause in Todra Gorge before continuing east to the dunes of Erg Chebbi.
Around Merzouga
Choose village visits or a walk among the dunes, or enjoy a quiet day at your accommodation.
Merzouga → Ouarzazate
Return through the southern valleys, stopping for the night near Ouarzazate.
Ouarzazate → Marrakech
Cross the High Atlas back to Marrakech, with pauses along the mountain road.
practical: The route spreads the approach over several nights. Your proposal will include the selected stays, kasbah visits, camp arrangements and driving estimates.

story:
An evening near Aït Ben Haddou, palms around Skoura, the changing shapes of the Dades Valley: this journey gives the approach to the Sahara its own time and attention.

Near Merzouga, two nights make space for village visits, dune walks and a quieter afternoon. The return is broken near Ouarzazate, so the final Atlas crossing has a day of its own.

title: From the Sahara to Essaouira
summary: An evening by the dunes, a road through southern Morocco and two nights beside the Atlantic. Eight days of desert and coast, beginning and ending in Marrakech.
fit: For travelers who want both desert and coast and enjoy a changing view from the road. Several days involve substantial driving.
itinerary: Marrakech → Dades
Cross the High Atlas and visit Aït Ben Haddou on the way to your first night in the Dades Valley.
Dades → Merzouga
Spend time in Todra Gorge, then continue toward Merzouga for an evening and overnight near the dunes.
Merzouga → Ouarzazate
Travel back through southern settlements and stop in Ouarzazate for the night.
Ouarzazate → Taroudant
Head west to Taroudant and spend the night around this walled southern city.
Taroudant → Essaouira
Continue toward the Atlantic and arrive in Essaouira for the first of two nights by the coast.
An open day in Essaouira
Wander the medina and ramparts, watch the fishing port at work or ask us to arrange a coastal activity.
Essaouira → Marrakech
Return through argan country to Marrakech, where you’ll spend your final night.
Marrakech & departure
Enjoy a last walk if time allows, then continue to your flight or onward journey.
practical: This route connects distant regions. If you prefer shorter drives, we can focus on either the Sahara or the coast and spend more time there.

story:
Travel through the Atlas and Todra Gorge to a Sahara overnight, then turn west through Ouarzazate and Taroudant. By Essaouira, mountain roads have given way to sea air and fishing boats.

Two nights on the coast leave a full day for the medina, ramparts and a long lunch near the port. There’s a good deal of ground to cover between these landscapes; the reward is seeing how different one part of Morocco feels from the next.

title: Tangier to Marrakech: Cities & Sahara
summary: From Tangier and Chefchaouen to Fes, the Sahara and Marrakech. Ten days following Morocco south, with time in the medinas and a full day near the dunes.
fit: For a north-to-south holiday that brings together Chefchaouen, Fes and the Sahara. Particularly convenient when arriving in Tangier and leaving from Marrakech.
itinerary: Arrive in Tangier
Arrive in Tangier, settle into your accommodation and enjoy a first look around the city as time allows.
Tangier → Chefchaouen
Travel into the Rif Mountains and spend the night in Chefchaouen, with its blue streets and hillside setting.
Chefchaouen → Fes
Continue south to Fes. A visit to Volubilis can be considered if the day’s timing allows.
Fes on foot
Explore the medina on foot, leaving time for the craft and architecture that catch your attention.
Fes → Merzouga
Make the long drive south through the Middle Atlas and Ziz Valley toward Merzouga.
A desert day
Spend the day among the dunes and nearby communities, with a second evening in the desert region.
Merzouga → Dades
Leave Merzouga and travel through Todra Gorge toward the Dades Valley.
Dades → Marrakech
Visit Aït Ben Haddou and cross the High Atlas into Marrakech.
Marrakech at your pace
Choose a medina walk, time in the gardens or a day exploring on your own.
Departure
Leave for your flight or onward journey, with the transfer arranged around your plans.
practical: Fes to Merzouga is a full day on the road. If you have more time, an overnight near Midelt can divide that drive and make the journey gentler.

Begin beside the Strait in Tangier before spending a night among Chefchaouen’s blue lanes. In Fes, a full day brings you closer to the workshops, courtyards and neighborhoods within the medina.

The route then turns south through the Ziz Valley to Merzouga. A desert day, Todra Gorge and the High Atlas lead you onward to Marrakech, without doubling back to your starting point.

title: Two Weeks Through Morocco
summary: Blue streets in the Rif, the medina of Fes, Sahara dunes and Atlantic mornings. Two weeks connecting Morocco’s cities and landscapes, with longer stays along the way.
fit: A first Morocco visit with two weeks to explore and an appetite for variety. Expect a substantial road journey, balanced by longer stays in several destinations.
itinerary: Casablanca → Rabat
Arrive in Casablanca and continue to Rabat, with any sightseeing arranged around your flight time.
Rabat → Chefchaouen
Travel north into the Rif and settle into Chefchaouen.
A day in Chefchaouen
Enjoy a full day among blue lanes, small squares and hillside viewpoints.
Chefchaouen → Fes
Continue to Fes, with a possible stop at Volubilis if the schedule allows.
A day in Fes
Discover the medina’s craft workshops, courtyards and food on foot.
Fes → Merzouga
Cross the Middle Atlas and follow the Ziz Valley toward Merzouga and the Sahara.
A day around Erg Chebbi
Explore the desert region at your own pace and spend a second night near Erg Chebbi.
Merzouga → Dades
Leave the dunes for Todra Gorge and an overnight in the Dades Valley.
Dades → Marrakech
Visit Aït Ben Haddou before crossing the High Atlas to Marrakech.
Marrakech on foot
Spend a day exploring Marrakech’s medina and gardens.
An open day in Marrakech
Try a cooking class, visit a hammam or leave the day free to follow your own interests.
Marrakech → Essaouira
Travel to Essaouira and settle into the slower rhythm of the coast.
A day in Essaouira
Explore the fishing port, walk the ramparts and browse the medina’s artisan streets.
Essaouira → Marrakech
Return to Marrakech with ample time for your departure. For an early flight, add a final night in the city.
practical: There are long driving days within this circuit. We’ll plan the final Essaouira-to-Marrakech transfer around your flight; an extra night in Marrakech is sensible for an early departure.

story:
There’s time here to see the country change: from Rabat and Chefchaouen to Fes, then through the mountains toward the Sahara. Full days in several stops let you do more than arrive, look around and leave.

After the desert and southern valleys, Marrakech brings gardens and lively souks. The journey finishes with Essaouira’s sea air before the return to Marrakech. It’s a wide-ranging first visit, with room to add a night wherever you’d like to linger.

title: A Day at Ouzoud Waterfalls
summary: Follow shaded paths through olive groves, pause above the cascades and enjoy lunch with the sound of falling water. A full day in the countryside from Marrakech, with transport arranged for your group.
fit: A day outdoors for couples, families and friends who enjoy scenery and walking. The route can be adapted, though some paths are steep and uneven.
itinerary: 08:30 · Set off from Marrakech
Your driver meets you at your accommodation or the nearest accessible meeting point. Settle in for the drive northeast, leaving the bustle of Marrakech behind.
Morning · Through the Tadla plains
Farmland and olive groves fill the view as you approach the Middle Atlas foothills. The journey takes around three hours, with a stop along the way to stretch your legs.
Around 11:30 · First views of Ouzoud
Arrive in Tanaghmeilt village and take in the waterfalls. Choose the walking route that suits you before beginning the descent into the gorge.
Late morning & afternoon · Beside the falls
Spend around four to five hours exploring, including time for lunch. Follow shaded paths between viewpoints, look for macaques in the trees and, if you wish, take a boat closer to the spray.
Lunch · A table by the cascades
Choose a café overlooking the water for a Moroccan lunch, or find a place to enjoy your picnic. Lunch, drinks and the optional boat ride are payable separately unless included in your quote.
Before 16:00 · Back through the village
Allow 20–30 minutes for the walk uphill, with a little time to browse the village stalls before meeting your driver.
Around 16:00 · The road home
Relax on the drive back, with a break along the way. You’ll reach your accommodation in Marrakech between 19:00 and 20:00, depending on traffic.
practical: Ouzoud is around 150 km from Marrakech, usually 2½–3 hours each way. Wear shoes with good grip: paths can be slippery, and the climb back takes 20–30 minutes. Swimming and boat trips depend on conditions. Watch the macaques from a distance and avoid feeding them.

story:
The sound of the falls reaches you before the view opens. Paths weave between fig and olive trees, revealing different angles on the cascades as you make your way into the gorge.

With four to five hours in the area, there’s time for the walk, a riverside lunch and an optional boat ride near the spray. The day unfolds at a comfortable pace, with room to stop and enjoy the surroundings.

title: A Day in the Ourika Valley
summary: Walnut trees, hillside villages and lunch beside the river. Leave Marrakech for the Ourika Valley, with a waterfall walk at Setti Fatma or a quieter afternoon by the water.
fit: For a change of scene close to Marrakech. Choose the waterfall trail for a more active outing, or spend your time in the village and beside the river.
itinerary: 09:00 · Leave Marrakech behind
Your driver meets you at your accommodation or a nearby accessible point. Head south toward the Atlas foothills as the city gives way to open countryside.
On the way · Meet the argan producers
Stop at a women’s cooperative to see how argan oil is made. There’s time to look around and browse the products if something catches your eye.
Around 10:00 · Along the Ourika River
Follow the valley past walnut trees, terraced fields and villages on the slopes. On Mondays, stop at Tnin Ourika’s weekly market for a glimpse of local life.
Setti Fatma · Waterfall or riverbank
Take the rocky path to the first waterfall, allowing around 45 minutes in each direction. Or stay in the village, explore its cafés and enjoy the river. We’ll arrange the day around your choice.
Lunch · Under the trees
Find a table beside the river for tagine or grilled dishes, with the water flowing nearby. Lunch and drinks are payable separately unless included in your quote.
Afternoon · A little time to linger
Browse the craft stalls or settle by the water. If you’d like to cool off in the river pools, check the local conditions first.
17:00–18:00 · Return to Marrakech
Enjoy the views on the drive back down the valley. Your driver brings you to your accommodation or the return point agreed for the day.
practical: The waterfall trail is rocky and can be steep or slippery, so walking shoes are essential. Staying by the river is the gentler option; let us know which you prefer when planning your day.

As the road follows the river into the Atlas foothills, Marrakech begins to feel a world away. Terraced fields and villages line the valley, and the cafés at Setti Fatma invite you to stay for lunch.

Walk up to the first waterfall if you’d like a more active day, or keep to the village and riverbank. Either way, there’s time to enjoy the scenery without hurrying from one stop to the next.

title: Essaouira, a Day by the Sea
summary: Blue fishing boats, sea-facing ramparts and a medina made for wandering. Spend a day on the Atlantic coast, with time for a seafood lunch and a walk along the shore.
fit: For a taste of the coast during a Marrakech stay. There are roughly three hours of travel each way, with around four hours to enjoy Essaouira.
itinerary: 08:30 · Toward the Atlantic
Meet your driver at your accommodation and head west across the Haouz plains. The coast is your destination today, with a few pauses along the way.
Morning · Coffee & argan country
Stop for coffee in Chichaoua, then visit a women’s cooperative to see the traditional extraction of argan oil. Continue through the argan-growing countryside toward the sea.
Around 12:00 · Welcome to Essaouira
Arrive near the medina entrance, with around four hours to explore. Wander independently or follow a medina visit arranged in advance.
Midday · Inside the sea walls
Follow narrow lanes past workshops and galleries, then walk the Skala ramparts for views of the Atlantic. Look out for thuya woodwork and silver jewelry along the way.
Lunch · Down by the harbor
Stroll among the blue fishing boats before choosing lunch near the port or in the medina. Grilled seafood is a natural choice here. Lunch is payable separately unless included in your quote.
Afternoon · Your time on the coast
Walk along the sandy beach, return to a favorite shop or enjoy mint tea on Place Moulay Hassan. Leave a little time simply to sit and watch the town go by.
Around 16:00 · Back to Marrakech
Your driver meets you near the medina entrance for the journey inland. With breaks along the way, expect to reach your accommodation between 19:00 and 20:00.
practical: Allow around three hours each way, depending on traffic and stops. Bring a layer for the Atlantic breeze. A medina visit can be arranged, and an overnight stay is an option if you’d like more time.

story:
Essaouira feels different from the moment you arrive: cooler air, gulls over the harbor and the Atlantic just beyond the medina walls. Walk between small workshops and galleries, then follow the boats to the fishing port.

The afternoon is yours to enjoy. Find a table for lunch, browse the souks or pause for mint tea on Place Moulay Hassan. Your driver takes care of the return to Marrakech; if a single day feels too short, ask us about staying overnight.

title: Across the Atlas to Aït Ben Haddou
summary: Wind through the High Atlas to Aït Ben Haddou’s earthen towers and the kasbahs of Ouarzazate. A full day of mountain views, village lanes and Morocco’s film country.
fit: For travelers drawn to architecture, film locations and mountain scenery, with a full day free and a liking for a scenic drive.
itinerary: Around 07:00 · Into the High Atlas
Your driver meets you at your accommodation for an early departure. Climb into the mountains past terraced hillsides and villages overlooking the road.
Morning · Tizi n’Tichka
Pause at viewpoints around the 2,260-metre pass. Take in the peaks and the road winding below before descending toward the southern kasbahs.
Midday · The lanes of Aït Ben Haddou
Explore the fortified village on foot, following earthen lanes toward the granary at the top. Enjoy the valley views and look for settings you may recognize from film and television.
Afternoon · Ouarzazate & its film studios
Continue to Ouarzazate and Taourirt Kasbah. If you’ve chosen to visit the Atlas Film Studios, explore the sets along the way. Studio admission is an optional extra.
Lunch · A pause in Ouarzazate
Take a seat at a local restaurant for tagine, couscous or grilled dishes. Lunch and drinks are payable separately unless included in your quote.
Afternoon · The mountain road home
Cross the Atlas once more, with a different light on the slopes. A stop at an argan cooperative can be added on request if time allows.
Around 19:00 · Back in Marrakech
Return to your accommodation or agreed meeting point, with the evening ahead after a full day in the mountains.
practical: Expect an early start, an evening return and winding mountain roads. Comfortable shoes are best for the uneven lanes and uphill walk. Monument tickets, meals and any local assistance will be detailed in your quote; the film studios are optional. Weather and road conditions may affect the schedule.

The Atlas crossing offers a changing view at every turn: hillside villages, cultivated terraces and peaks rising above the road. Beyond the pass, Aït Ben Haddou stands in warm earth against the valley.

Explore its lanes and climb toward the old granary before continuing to Ouarzazate and Taourirt Kasbah. Film lovers can add a visit to the Atlas studios. It’s a long day, but a striking introduction to the landscapes south of Marrakech.

title: An Evening in Agafay
summary: Watch the light soften over Agafay’s rocky hills, then settle in for an evening meal. Open skies and desert scenery, within an evening’s reach of Marrakech.
fit: An easy change of scene for a free evening in Marrakech, especially if you’d like desert landscapes without a multi-day journey.

Leave Marrakech for your chosen venue in Agafay. Arrive with time to settle in and enjoy the open landscape.
Golden hour · Make it yours
Find a viewpoint as the light changes across the hills, or enjoy a camel or quad session arranged separately.
Evening · Dinner & return
Sit down to dinner at the selected venue, then return to Marrakech at the agreed time.
practical: Agafay is a rocky desert, distinct from the Sahara’s sand dunes. Your venue, menu, drinks, optional activities and return time are agreed before booking.

story:
Beyond Marrakech, the stone desert opens into low hills and a wide horizon. Arrive with time to take in the late-afternoon light before dinner at your chosen venue.

You can keep the evening simple—a view, a meal and time together—or add a camel ride or quad outing. We’ll help you choose the setting and agree the details before you go.

title: Imlil & the Atlas, by Way of Agafay
summary: Rocky desert, lake views and a walk among mountain villages. Follow the road from Agafay through Lalla Takerkoust and the Kik Plateau to Imlil, with a camel ride and lunch along the way.
fit: For travelers who enjoy a varied day outdoors, with a one- to two-hour mountain walk. We’ll plan the trail and camel ride around your group’s comfort.
itinerary: 09:00 · From Marrakech to Agafay
Your driver meets you for the day’s journey by 4×4. Head southwest, stopping to take in the views as farmland gives way to Agafay’s rocky hills.
Morning · A camel ride in Agafay
Join the camel team for an hour among stony hills and dry valleys, with the Atlas Mountains stretching across the horizon.
Lalla Takerkoust · Beside the lake
Pause by the water for photographs and a quiet moment before the road begins to climb.
Kik Plateau · Mountain views & mint tea
Look out over terraces and hillside settlements, then visit a Berber family for mint tea and homemade bread. On Saturdays, the route also takes in Asni’s weekly market.
Afternoon · On foot around Imlil
Begin a one- to two-hour walk through walnut terraces, hamlets and streams toward the waterfalls. The pace is set to suit your group.

Enjoy a three-course Moroccan lunch in Imlil with views over the valley: salad, tagine or couscous, followed by fruit and mint tea.

Return through Moulay Brahim Gorge and the Asni area. The drive takes around an hour and a half, bringing you back to Marrakech for the evening.
